'''Barbarian Village''' is a small village south of [[Edgeville]] and west of [[Varrock]]. The entire village is a [[multicombat area]] containing many [[aggressive]] [[barbarian]]s, so low level players are advised to proceed with caution. Players can enter the [[Stronghold of Security]] through a hole in the centre of the village.

==Transportation==
Several transport options bring players into or close to Barbarian Village, listed here with their arrival destination. From closest to farthest:

* {{plink|Skull sceptre}} — [[Stronghold of Security]] entrance.
* {{plink|Canoe|pic=Paddle}} — Barbarian Village station. Requires 12 [[Woodcutting]].
* {{plink|Skills necklace}} — [[Cooking Guild]], just east of the village.
* {{plink|Amulet of glory}} — Edgeville centre, just north of the village.
* {{plink|Minigame teleport|pic=Minigame icon}} — [[Soul Wars]], which has a [[Soul Wars Portal|portal]] to [[Edgeville]].
* {{plink|Varrock Teleport}} — center of [[Varrock]], well east of the village.

==History==
{{LoreSources|Varrock Museum|the1=yes}}

Almost 200 years ago, the lost art of [[Runecraft]] was rediscovered, allowing humans to quickly dominate most of [[Gielinor]], and marking the start of the [[Fifth Age]]. The nomadic mountain tribes of [[Rellekka]] embarked on a [[Runecrafting Crusades|crusade]] to stop the use of Magic and Runecrafting, which they believe belong only to the [[gods]]. During this time, the first [[Wizards' Tower]] was burned to the ground (although not by the barbarians), and the magic-using [[Imcando dwarf|Imcando dwarves]] were driven to near-extinction.

As casualties mounted, however, the tribes dwindled and were dispersed, and the Barbarian Village was established in between what is now [[Varrock]] and [[Falador]] as a temporary outpost until the tribes could recover their numbers. Over time, the barbarians gradually settled down, and the village became a more permanent establishment.

=== Skill training spots ===
Despite its small size, the village has a number of useful training spots and facilities:

* The [[barbarian anvil]] can be used to make [[hastae]] after completing [[barbarian training]].
* The [[Barbarian Village mine]] at the centre of the village contains [[coal]] and [[Tin ore|tin]].
* Players can fish with [[feather]]s or [[fishing bait]] at the [[Fishing spots]] east of the village, requiring level 20 and 25 [[Fishing]].
* There is a [[Permanent fire|never-ending fire]] west of the fishing spots, which is popular among [[free-to-play]] players for quickly cooking caught fish. There are also perpetually burning fires in the middle of Peksa's shop and at the end of the [[The Long Hall|longhall]].
* The village is useful for [[Crafting]] training at low levels. Players can use [[soft clay]] with the [[Potter's Wheel|Potter's wheel]] and the [[pottery oven]] nearby to craft pottery items. In the free worlds, this is the only location of a potter's wheel and oven outside of the [[Crafting Guild]]. There is also a [[spinning wheel]] that can be used to make [[balls of wool]] and other spun items.

===Stronghold of Security===
{{Main|Stronghold of Security}}
Reached through a hole located in the mining area, the [[Stronghold of Security]], released on [[Update:Security and free-to-play update - the Stronghold of Security|4 July 2006]], is open to both [[members]] and [[free-to-play]] players. The medium-sized dungeon gives rewards for making it to the centre of each of its four levels, each of increasing difficulty. Various [[monsters]] inhabit each level, including [[goblin]]s, [[skeleton]]s, [[ankou]], and several monsters unique to the dungeon, such as [[Minotaur|minotaurs]].

=== Personalities ===

* {{Chatl|Atlas}}, a skilled physical trainer.
* {{Chatl|Checkal}}, a self-absorbed bodybuilder.
* {{Chatl|Hunding}}, an aloof barbarian who will share the village's history if asked nicely.
* {{Chatl|Litara}}, a barbarian waiting for her deceased brother [[Solztun]] to return from the [[Stronghold of Security]].
* {{Chatl|Peksa}}, a helmet merchant.
* {{Chatl|Sigurd}}, a [[canoe]] tutor.
* {{Chatl|Tassie Slipcast}}, a non-barbarian potter who opened her studio on a loan.
